text:
The Mammoth are 13-10-3, 3-4-3 in their last ten, and that is the frustrating part: they have been one of the stronger teams in the league on process. Utah owns 54.5% of expected goals (the quality of chances each side gets) and 57% at five on five. The goaltending has handed back the difference, about 11 more goals allowed than the chances against predict, and our numbers say the Mammoth are about 3.2 points short of what they deserved. Playoff odds: 68%.

The net is the story. KSL Sports asked out loud whether Sebastian Cossa is ready to be the No. 1, and Karel Vejmelka has had nights like Monday, when he was the first goalie off. Wednesday's 4-3 win over Minnesota ended the Wild's 15-game point streak and Kirill Kaprizov's, a reminder of what this team looks like when the saves show up.

Logan Cooley is the one doing the most: 16 points in his last ten, above the 10.7 his chances suggest. Vincent Trocheck has centered him, and the third line of Anders Lee, Kailer Yamamoto and Barrett Hayton has quietly taken 73% of the chances. Jack McBain has become the enforcer people write about after fighting Gabriel Landeskog and drawing a Player Safety review for his hit on Gavin Brindley. MacKenzie Weegar and Mikhail Sergachev are the top pair. André Tourigny's team is doing the hard part. It needs a goalie to finish it.
headline: Utah plays better than its record
